title: Price Drift before U.S. Macroeconomic News: Private Information about Public Announcements?
one_line: For 9 of 20 market-moving US releases (2008-2014), ES and Treasury futures start moving the 'right' way ~30 minutes before the release, about 40% of the total move on average — consistent with leakage or proprietary nowcasting.

findings.statement: Pre-release drift for 9 of 20 market-moving announcements, starting ~30 minutes before.
Drift ≈ 49% of the total move for stocks, 36% for bonds; significant for ES on pending home sales, ISM non-manufacturing, ISM manufacturing, existing home sales.
Stronger for non-government releasers and pre-released/embargoed data.

why.pattern: Informed trading before public releases (leakage / superior proprietary forecasting).
why.mechanism: Some traders know or predict the number and trade before release; prices drift toward the outcome.

reported_results.headline: Pre-release drift ≈ 40% of the total move for 9 of 20 releases.

tradable_edge: Not directly tradable (the direction is the surprise, unknown in advance). Possible angle: trade WITH a strong 30-minute pre-release move into ISM/home-sales releases — speculative; also a warning to avoid entries just before those releases.
angles: Event filter: avoid new entries 30 minutes before ISM / home-sales releases

decay_risk.reason: Release procedures tightened after 2013 (pre-release lock-ups ended).

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Strategy would need second-level data and a release calendar.
Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 2), not by the weekly pipeline.
